newsitem.title: USA: IMF expected to approve release of funds to Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF expected to approve release of funds to Russia.

text.p: The IMF is expected to approve the release of further funding for Russia shortly after the country took tough action to revamp its economy, international monetary sources said on Monday.
The sources, who declined to be named, said the decision could come as soon as Friday, when the International Monetary Fund's board is tentatively slated to discuss the issue.
"The situation basically looks all right," one source said.
It was not immediately clear how much money would be involved, but sources said the board is likely to approve the release of at least one loan tranche worth some $350 million.
The financing would be made available under a $10 billion stand-by loan agreement struck between Russia and the Fund last year.

The IMF delayed payment of several tranches of that loan in the second half of last year because tax revenues were well below budgeted levels, threatening to undermine government finances, and because the government was slow to meet reform promises.
While the government's fiscal position, in the words of one source, remains "difficult," tax collections picked up in December, apparently to the satisfaction of the IMF.
Where there were problems, however, was in the area of structural reform. The IMF in the past has sharply criticized Russia for dragging its heels in carrying out such reforms.
To address those concerns and obtain approval for further funding, Moscow took some tough steps recently to restructure its economy in the face of stiff domestic opposition.
It scrapped plans for quotas on vodka imports, instead introducing a simple licensing procedure to register importers.

It also adopted a new pricing procedure for natural gas sales and sharply cut back on the list of so-called strategic consumers of energy whose supplies cannot be cut off even if they fail to pay their bills.
